paper_metadata.title: Quantum Optimization for Network Capacity Expansion of Microgrid Models via Grover-Enhanced QAOA

summary: The paper evaluates a Grover-mixer QAOA on an 11-variable microgrid expansion MILP mapped to 11 qubits and simulated with 5000 shots on a noiseless Qiskit Aer statevector simulator. The classical optimum bitstring (11110111011, cost −5) appears with probability 0.0166 at depth p=1, peaks at 0.1730 at p=3, and drops to 0.1172 at p=4, while the classical Gurobi solver deterministically finds the optimum. The work demonstrates feasibility amplification within QAOA but no computational advantage.

experiments.description: Grover-enhanced QAOA on an 11-binary-variable microgrid network expansion instance derived from a PyPSA model, evaluated at QAOA depths 1-4 using noiseless statevector simulation and 5000-shot sampling; compared against a classical Gurobi optimum.

hyperparameters.beta_parameterization: integer Grover iteration counts per layer

algorithm.parameter_initialization: coarse grid search over discrete beta vectors, then refine gamma with L-BFGS-B; initial state is uniform superposition H^⊗n|0⟩^⊗n

optimizer_settings.parameter_bounds: gamma in (0, pi]; beta as nonnegative integers

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary decision variable; 11 binary variables encode modular generation capacity, branch capacity increments, conductor selectors, and load-connection decisions
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Linear equality/inequality constraints enforced by a Grover-style feasibility oracle; soft penalty added to objective for feasible mass below threshold tau
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Diagonal cost Hamiltonian with single-qubit Z terms; implementation uses H_impl = 15 I + sum_i a_i Z_i with a = [1,2,0,0,6,0,0,1,-5,-5,-5]

problem_instance.description: Small representative distribution-network microgrid expansion problem modeled in PyPSA with 3 buses and candidate generators/branches; benchmarked against a Gurobi global optimum

dataset_specification.description: 11-variable MILP derived from a minimal distribution network with buses B0-B2, candidate generator at B0, branch capacity choices, conductor selectors, and served-load variables

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical MILP solved to global optimality with Gurobi; feasible binary assignments enumerated for benchmarking
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Noiseless statevector simulation plus 5000-shot sampling; results reported for QAOA depths 1, 2, 3, and 4; compared to classical optimum 11110111011

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Solve MILP with Gurobi; enumerate feasible binary assignments; construct diagonal cost observable and Grover feasibility oracle
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute expected cost from statevector probabilities; draw 5000 samples to estimate empirical frequencies, feasible mass, and probability of the classical optimum

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: grid search over discrete beta values followed by L-BFGS-B refinement of gamma; reported performance at depths 1-4

speedup_claims.conditions: Proof-of-concept benchmark on a single 11-variable instance using noiseless statevector simulation and 5000-shot sampling
speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or empirical speedup is claimed; the paper reports improved probability mass on the optimum, not runtime advantage.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: not identified; only a single 11-variable instance evaluated
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Unknown; would require substantially larger problem sizes, deeper QAOA circuits, and fault-tolerant hardware capable of implementing Grover-oracle feasibility checks for large MILPs.
limiting_factors: Evaluation limited to a single 11-variable instance (2^11 search space).
All results obtained on a noiseless statevector simulator rather than real hardware.
Classical MILP solver (Gurobi) finds the exact optimum deterministically and efficiently.
No runtime comparison or complexity scaling demonstrating advantage.
Grover-based mixer requires feasibility oracle construction which may scale poorly for larger constrained problems.

notes: circuit_depth is inferred because the paper reports QAOA layer counts (1-4) rather than a single compiled depth value.
speedup_order is inferred as none_proven because the paper provides only a proof-of-concept benchmark and no asymptotic complexity or speedup claim.
Authors do not claim quantum advantage; they benchmark against a Gurobi optimum and report probability amplification of the optimal bitstring rather than runtime improvement.
Classical solver already computes the global optimum directly, so the quantum method does not outperform the baseline.
